incidents.name: Lodestar plvGLP exchange-rate manipulation
incidents.notes: The lending market behaved as designed; Lodestar's plvGLP oracle derived the collateral price from the GlpDepositor's assets-per-share ratio, and the attacker inflated that ratio with GlpDepositor.donate() so a flash-loaned plvGLP position could borrow out the other Lodestar markets.

sources.ref: onchain review: lplvGLP market 0xcc25dac54a1a62061b596fd3baf7d454f34c56ff created 2022-11-21 by 0x67e57a0ec37768eaf99a364975ec4e1f98920d01 (Lodestar deployer), unrelated to attack sender 0xc29d94386ff784006ff8461c170d1953cc9e2b5c; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events, so the market code was 18.9 days old; reported attacker profit ~$6.5M against ~$6.9M of protocol loss Recheck of the deployment basis (DELEGATECALL audit): the victim is a Compound-fork CErc20Delegator, whose implementation lives in plain storage slot 18 rather than an EIP-1967 slot; binary-searching eth_getStorageAt on slot 18 over [40021576, 45121904] shows it holds 0x4eb611232ce3a738d9ee20467a5dd2ecf3b2d919 unchanged from creation to the incident (no NewImplementation in the window), the delegator runtime is byte-identical at both blocks, and the CToken implementation itself contains no DELEGATECALL, so the executing code dates from deployment.
